paper_title: WebGLM Towards An Efficient Web-Enhanced Question Answering System with   Human Preferences
caption: retriever time analysis.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the time distribution across four stages—Search, Fetch, Extract, and Retrieval—of a retriever component in the WebGLM system, measured in seconds (sec.) across four performance percentiles: Avg., 50%, 75%, and 90%. The vertical axis ranges from 0.0 to 8.0 seconds with tick marks at 2.0-second intervals, while the horizontal axis lists the four percentile categories. Each bar is stacked to show the cumulative contribution of each stage: Search (dark blue), Fetch (medium blue), Extract (light blue), and Retrieval (very light blue). At the average level, total time is approximately 5.5 seconds, with Search contributing ~1.8s, Fetch ~2.2s, Extract ~1.0s, and Retrieval ~0.5s. At the 50th percentile, total time is ~3.5s, with similar proportional contributions. At the 75th percentile, total time rises to ~5.5s, and at the 90th percentile, it reaches ~8.5s, dominated by Fetch (~4.5s) and Search (~2.0s), with Extract and Retrieval adding smaller increments. The chart visually emphasizes that Fetch and Search are the most time-consuming stages, especially at higher percentiles, while Extract and Retrieval remain relatively constant and minor contributors.
